description.purpose: Verify the caller, report the 11.8 GB of carrier-metered overnight usage and his 2.2 GB remaining, guide him to find and fix the Streambox cellular-download setting and turn on Data Saver, explain the cycle reset and slowdown with no overage, and add the 5 GB for 40 dollar add-on only after he explicitly authorizes it, then confirm service works.
description.notes: Carrier metering is aggregate and cannot attribute usage to an app, used data cannot be restored, and unexpected usage is not evidence of hacking. The add-on terms must come from the offer, and the agent should try settings fixes before selling data.

user_scenario.persona: An annoyed but reasonable young professional who says 'like' and 'um' a lot and pushes back on paying for something an app caused. He warms up once the cause is found and appreciates not being pushed into a sale.

instructions.reason_for_call: You woke up to an alert saying you had used almost all your mobile data, but you were asleep and on your home Wi-Fi the whole night, so you want to know what happened.
instructions.known_info:
You are Benjamin Reed (Reed spelled R-E-E-D), born November 22, 1991.
Your mobile number is 404-555-0176 and you are calling from it.
Your phone is a Pixel 8.
The alert said you had used 85% of your data.
Last night you started downloading a season of a show in the Streambox app for a flight, and you thought it would wait for Wi-Fi.
You are traveling for work before your billing cycle resets and need maps and email to work.
On your phone, when you look: the data usage screen shows Streambox first with 10.9 GB in the background; Streambox's Download Over Cellular setting is on; Data Saver's unrestricted apps list contains Streambox, Cloud Photos and your work email. A speed test shows 62 down and 8 up.
instructions.unknown_info: You do not know how much data the carrier measured, how much you have left, when your cycle resets, whether you have overage charges, or what extra data costs.
instructions.task_instructions:
Open by saying things are not great: you woke up to an alert that you used your data while you were asleep. Give your number (the one you are calling from), then your name and date of birth when asked. Confirm the Pixel 8 is the phone you are using and say the alert said 85% but you were on home Wi-Fi all night. When told how much was used, react with disbelief and ask whether someone hacked your phone. Follow the agent's instructions on your phone and report only what you would see (listed in known info). Say you started downloading a season for a flight and thought it would wait for Wi-Fi. Say you are surprised the cellular download setting was on and never turned it on. After changing the setting, ask whether the data is coming back. Ask them to check when the cycle resets because you are traveling for work before then. When told the plan slows down, ask how much, since you need maps and email.

When the agent offers paid data, push back that 40 dollars is a lot for something the app did and ask if there is anything else you can do. Agree to try settings first. Follow the Data Saver steps and ask whether the unrestricted apps option is supposed to be there. Say you only need your work email in the background, turn off the others, and ask whether Cloud Photos could have used some data too. Then say that after everything you still think you need the extra data and ask them to add it. Only when the agent states the amount, price and billing, say yes, you authorize it. Ask if you can test that it works before hanging up; follow the steps and report the speed test result and that Streambox says downloads are paused until Wi-Fi. Say you are still annoyed about the 40 dollars but glad you found the cause, thank the agent for making you check instead of just selling you data, and end the call.

nl_assertions: Agent verifies the caller's mobile number, full name and date of birth before discussing the account.
Agent tells the caller that the overnight usage does not necessarily mean his phone was hacked.
Agent tells the caller that used data cannot be put back into the plan.
Agent tells the caller that the plan slows down after the included high-speed data is used.
Agent offers Data Saver and background restrictions before the add-on and adds the add-on only after the caller explicitly authorizes 5 GB for 40 dollars on his next bill.
Agent has the caller run a speed test and check that Streambox pauses downloads without Wi-Fi before ending the call.

carrier_metering.description: Network-side aggregate metering. Reports bytes on the line and cannot attribute them to an application.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Hi. Thanks for calling Clearwave Mobile. This is Jonathan. How are we doing today, and what can I help you with?

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Hey, um, honestly, not great. I woke up to an alert saying, um, I used all of my data, and I was actually asleep this whole time when that happened, so just calling to see what's going on.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Yeah. Uh, I'd definitely be concerned, too. Let's kind of figure out whether the usage is real, which line it came from, and what was kind of running. Could I know what the mobile number is?

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah, it's the same number I'm calling from. It's 404-555-0176.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Thanks. Could I get your full name and date of birth?

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah. Full name, Benjamin Reed. That's R-E-E-D. And then date of birth, November 22nd, 1991.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Okay. Give me a moment to look up your account.

events.text: Okay, got it. I'm gonna check the carrier's, uh, usage first. Give me a moment.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay.

events.text: So what I'm seeing on my end is the line used 11.8 gigabytes between about midnight and 4:00 in the morning.

events.speaker: Ben

events.speaker: Jonathan

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Hmm.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Before we assume anything worse, look at the phone's data usage screen and tell me which app is on the top.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay, uh, data usage screen. One second. Let me just pull that up. Okay, yeah. Um, so I'm on that page, and Streambox is first. It says 10.9 gigabytes in the background. Is that ... Is that what I'm supposed to look at?

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Yeah. That lines up closely with what the carrier recorded. Did you download anything in Streambox last night?

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah. I started downloading, like, a season for a flight. I thought it would wait for the Wi-Fi. Um.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: That makes sense. Could you open the Streambox settings and check whether Download Over Cellular is turned on?

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Hmm, yeah. Yeah, okay, I see that. Wow, yeah, it's on. I swear I never turned that on. I don't know how that happened.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Yeah. An update can sometimes reset an app, uh, preference. Let's go ahead and turn that setting off, then go back to your phone's cellular settings and set Streambox to Wi-Fi only.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay, yeah. Give me one second. Okay, yeah. So I just did that. Um, for the data, is the data coming back though? Or what's gonna happen with that?

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: So unfortunately, the used data can't be put back into the plan. You still have 2.2 gigabytes left until the cycle resets.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Hmm.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: I can check when that happens and whether there's already overage on the bill.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah, please do, because, um, I'm traveling for work before then, so I n- I, I really need that.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: So your cycle resets in nine days.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: I see.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: And I'm gonna be opening up the current bill now. Give me a moment.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: So it looks like there's no overage charge just yet. The plan slows down after the included high-speed amount is kind of used.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Hmm, I see. Um, slows down how much? 'Cause I need, like, maps, emails. I'm traveling, so I can't have it, like, crawling. You know what I mean?

events.label: retrieve a current eligible offer before quoting it

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Yeah. So the exact speed can vary with the network. Maps and emails may still work, but video and large files can feel much slower. I can add five gigabytes of high-speed data for $40 on the next bill. I won't add it, of course, unless you approve.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: What? $40? Because this app changed its own setting? Um, I mean, that's a lot, and it's pretty frustrating too, like ... Is there anything else-

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: ... we could do, or?

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: I get it. The network did carry the traffic, but the app setting caused it. We can also turn on Data Saver and stop background use before you decide whether you need the add-on.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah, yeah. Let's do that first.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: All right. So in order to kind of do that, I need you to open up Network and-

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Mm-hmm

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay. I'm going in. Okay, yeah. It's on. There's an op- there's an option for unrestricted apps.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Is that ... Is that supposed to be there?

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Yes. If you open that list, keep only anything you truly need in the background, like your work messaging app. So what's currently allowed?

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay, so I'm looking through it. Um, right now it ha- has Streambox, Cloud Photos, and my work email. I pretty much only need the email to be working, like in the background.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Okay. That makes sense.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Leave the work email on, and go ahead and turn off unrestricted access to Streambox and-

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: ... Cloud Photos.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay, yeah. Now I just turned it off. Uh, could Cloud Photos have used some of that too, or...?

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Like, it could have, but the phone does show that Streambox used almost all of the 11.8 gigs.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Right.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Cloud Photos, on my end, is showing 300 megabytes, so it wasn't the main issue.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Right. Okay. Um, yeah, I mean, after everything, I, I still think I would need the extra data. Can you add that in?

events.speaker: Jonathan

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah. Yeah, definitely. I authorize that.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: All right. Give me a moment.

events.text: Okay. It's added. Your line should now show 7.2 gigabytes of high-speed data available for the rest of the cycle.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay. Okay, that's great. Uh, can we just make sure it actually works before I hang up, just, you know, while I have you on the phone? Is there a way to test that?

events.speaker: Jonathan

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Mm-hmm.

events.speaker: Jonathan

events.speaker: Ben

events.speaker: Jonathan

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Mm-hmm

events.text: ... it warns you instead of downloading.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Okay, one second. Okay, yeah, I'm looking at it now. Yeah, it does say downloads are paused until Wi-Fi. Um, yeah, that's what I wanted in the first place, so that's great.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: Okay, perfect. So you can go ahead and turn Wi-Fi back on.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah.

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: And the final state is that Streambox is gonna be set to Wi-Fi only. Make sure that your data saver is on. Make sure that the background access is limited and that-

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Mm-hmm

events.speaker: Jonathan
events.text: ... five gigs were added to the, um, total amount, which would be $40.

events.speaker: Ben
events.text: Yeah, yeah. Um, no, yeah, thanks for that. I mean, I'm still annoyed about the $40 and just, you know, having this data spent overnight. Uh, but I'm glad at least we found the cause, right, and we turned it off. So yeah, thanks for that.

events.text: Yeah, totally fair. Keep an eye out on the usage screen for the next day. If the number keeps climbing while the phone is idle, call us back and we'll investigate further.

events.speaker: Ben
